items.title: Articular involvement in antiphospholipid syndrome: Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characterization.
items.abstract: IntroductionAntiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is characterized by antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) and thrombotic and/or obstetric events. Musculoskeletal manifestations, particularly arthralgia, are frequently reported, although their clinical and pathophysiological correlates remain incompletely characterized.ObjectiveTo characterize the clinical, laboratory, and imaging features of articular involvement in primary and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated APS compared with healthy controls.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 99 participants aged 18-50 years: 38 with primary APS (PAPS), 26 with APS associated with SLE (APS/SLE), and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. APS patients fulfilled the Sydney classification criteria, and those with SLE were classified according to the 1997 American College of Rheumatology criteria. Arthralgia was clinically assessed. Radiographic and high-resolution ultrasound (US) evaluation of the hands and wrists was performed. Laboratory tests included erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies.ResultsAge was comparable across groups ( p = 0.206). In the comparative analysis of aPL profiles between PAPS and APS/SLE, lupus anticoagulant was the most prevalent antibody in both groups (94.7% vs 96.2%; p = 0.792). IgG anticardiolipin and anti-β 2 -glycoprotein I antibodies were more frequent in PAPS (42.1% vs 15.4%, p = 0.024; 32.4% vs 0%, p = 0.019). Arthralgia was more frequent in APS/SLE than in PAPS (80.8% vs 50%; p = 0.013), as was morning stiffness (46.2% vs 21.1%; p = 0.033). ESR levels were higher in APS/SLE compared with PAPS and controls (median 19.5 vs 14 vs 6 mm/h; p < 0.001). CRP levels did not differ significantly among groups ( p = 0.118). RF positivity was low (2.6% in PAPS) and did not differ among groups (p = 1.000), and anti-CCP IgG antibodies were absent in all groups. Radiographic findings were mild and comparable. On US, joint effusion was more frequent in APS/SLE than in PAPS and controls (26.9% vs 2.6% vs 2.9%, respectively; p = 0.001), whereas synovitis, tenosynovitis, Power Doppler signal, and other findings showed no significant differences.ConclusionArticular manifestations are common in APS, particularly in APS/SLE, but are not consistently supported by objective evidence of inflammation. This dissociation suggests that musculoskeletal involvement may not be primarily mediated by overt inflammatory mechanisms.

items.title: Biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in Brazilian women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: BackgroundSystemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), a chronic autoimmune disease that predominantly affects women, can alter both physical appearance and bodily functioning through its manifestations and treatment, posing challenges to body image. Although body image in SLE has been associated with clinical, psychological, and sociodemographic factors, few studies have examined these domains simultaneously in women with SLE within a biopsychosocial framework, which limits understanding of their joint contributions.ObjectiveTo examine biopsychosocial factors associated with body image in a Brazilian sample of women with SLE.MethodsA nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted with 597 women with SLE. Participants provided sociodemographic and clinical information and completed the Body Esteem Scale for Adults and Adolescents (BESAA), Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS), and Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21). Bivariate associations were examined with nonparametric tests, and independent associations were examined with a hierarchical multiple linear regression including theoretically pre-specified sociodemographic, clinical, and psychological blocks.ResultsIn bivariate analyses, poorer body image was associated with active disease, skin lesions, joint pain, serous membrane inflammation, fever without infection, lower life satisfaction, higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress, lower educational attainment, and lower household income. The final model explained 35.4% of the variance in body image, with psychological variables accounting for 17.7% beyond sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. Greater life satisfaction and unintentional weight loss were independently associated with more positive body image, whereas higher levels of depression, skin lesions, and joint pain were independently associated with poorer body image.ConclusionsBody image in women with SLE is associated with factors across different biopsychosocial domains, suggesting that it should not be examined solely from a clinical perspective. Rather, psychological and social factors should be considered alongside disease-related characteristics to support more comprehensive approaches to the assessment and care of body image concerns in this population.

items.title: Pretreatment calprotectin level as a potential predictor of therapeutic response to tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis patients.
items.abstract: To promote a treat-to-target goal, there are unmet needs to identify the predictors of therapeutic response. Given a pathogenic role of calprotectin in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), we aimed to assess the predictability of pretreatment calprotectin levels for therapeutic response to tofacitinib, a Janus kinase inhibitor, in RA patients. We enrolled 51 patients receiving 24-week tofacitinib therapy and 25 healthy controls (HCs). RA activity was assessed using the 28-joint disease activity score-erythrocyte sedimentation rate (DAS28-ESR), and therapeutic response was evaluated using target attainment dichotomy. Plasma calprotectin levels were measured using the BÜHLMANN-sCAL® turbo turbidimetric assay. Twenty-eight (54.9%) patients were classified as the responders with combining remission and low-disease activity, and 23 (45.1%) as the non-responders with post-treatment DAS28-ESR > 3.2. Patients exhibited significantly higher calprotectin levels compared to HCs (median, 0.88 μg/mL vs. 0.24 μg/mL; p < 0.0001), and the non-responders had non-significant higher calprotectin levels compared to the responders (1.70 μg/mL vs. 0.58 μg/mL, p = 0.094). Pretreatment calprotectin levels were positively correlated with baseline DAS28 scores (r = 0.408, p = 0.003) and ESR (r = 0.374, p = 0.007). Plasma calprotectin levels significantly declined in the responders (median 0.58 μg/mL vs. 0.38 μg/mL, p < 0.01) after 24-week tofacitinib therapy, whereas no significant change in non-responders (1.70 μg/mL vs. 1.19 μg/mL, p = 0.601). The ROC analysis showed an AUC of 0.732 (95% CI 0.586-0.879) for calprotectin (cut-off 0.98 μg/mL; 73.9% sensitivity; 75.0% specificity). Its AUC significantly exceeded ESR (Holm-adjusted p = 0.039), but not CRP or DAS28-ESR. Pretreatment calprotectin level serves as a potential predictor of tofacitinib response, with higher levels indicating a lower likelihood of favorable response.

items.title: Gout as a risk factor for lower-extremity amputation in diabetes: a nationwide, register-based case-control study.
items.abstract: Non-healing diabetic foot ulcers are a major precursor to lower-extremity amputation (LEA) in diabetes, and gout may be an overlooked contributor. We hypothesised that individuals with both diabetes and gout have a higher risk of LEA than those with diabetes alone, with the strongest effect at more distal amputation levels. In a nationwide case-control study of 601,541 individuals with type 2 diabetes, we identified 4912 cases with LEA and 39,101 age- and sex-matched control participants. Gout exposure was determined using ICD-10 diagnoses and Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical codes for urate-lowering therapy. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression, adjusting for diabetes duration, peripheral arterial disease, acute myocardial infarction and late diabetes complications. Gout was associated with an increased risk of LEA (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.69, 2.02) in unadjusted analyses, and the association remained significant after full adjustment (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.37, 1.69). A significant trend (p=0.03) was observed across amputation levels, with potentially higher risk at more anatomically distal sites although no statistically significant differences were observed between individual amputation levels: OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.12, 1.68) for above-knee amputations, increasing to OR 1.65 (95% CI 1.32, 2.05) for toe amputations. Co-existing gout is an independent risk factor for LEA in individuals with type 2 diabetes. The risk is elevated across all amputation levels, with the most pronounced effect potentially being at distal anatomical sites. These findings highlight the need for increased awareness of gout when managing individuals with type 2 diabetes at risk of LEA.

items.title: Upadacitinib in Patients with Moderate-to-Severe Rheumatoid Arthritis: 2-Year Data from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland in the Observational UPHOLD Study.
items.abstract: Upadacitinib (UPA), an oral JAK inhibitor, has demonstrated efficacy and an acceptable safety profile in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) clinical trials, but real-world (RW) long-term data are limited. This sub-analysis of UPHOLD evaluated the long-term effectiveness and safety of UPA over 2 years in adults with moderate-to-severe RA in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. UPHOLD (NCT04497597) is an international, observational cohort study of adults with moderate-to-severe RA in whom the treating physician decided to initiate treatment with UPA 15 mg once daily prior to study enrollment. Effectiveness was assessed using disease activity measures, including the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints using C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP), as well as patient-reported outcomes (PROs). Endpoints were analyzed by modified nonresponder imputation (mNRI) and as observed (AO). All treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), including selected TEAEs of interest, are reported as exposure-adjusted event rates (events per 100 patient-years [E/100PY]). Of the 268 patients who were enrolled, 262 received at least one UPA dose and 150 (56.0%) completed 2 years. More than half achieved DAS28-CRP responses at month 6 (mNRI/AO remission, 58.8%/71.0%; and LDA, 66.3%/80.0%, respectively) and these responses were maintained through year 2 (mNRI/AO remission, 59.6%/82.4%; and LDA, 61.5%/89.3%, respectively). Among patients with available data at year 2, 68.3% achieved DAS28-CRP remission. Remission rates were consistent between monotherapy and combination therapy, regardless of prior treatments. Improvements in PROs were seen at 3 months and maintained or improved through 2 years. There were 435 TEAEs (50 serious). Due to the limited sample size and exposure time, caution is advised in interpreting safety; however, the safety profile was similar to prior phase 3 trials. UPA showed sustained effectiveness and a consistent safety profile over 2 years in routine RW practice. Among month-6 responders, remission was maintained through year 2 in the majority of patients. Among all patients assessed at year 2, two-thirds were in DAS28-CRP remission.

items.title: Effectiveness of Upadacitinib Versus Other Advanced Therapies in Rheumatoid Arthritis After Tumor Necrosis Factor Inhibitor Use in the United States.
items.abstract: Understanding comparative effectiveness of different biologic therapies in patients with inadequate response to a prior tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) may guide treatment decisions. This real-world analysis compared the clinical effectiveness of upadacitinib versus other advanced treatments (ATs), including TNFi, interleukin (IL)-6 inhibitors, and T cell co-stimulation modulators, in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who previously received a TNFi. This retrospective cohort study used data from the OM1 ® RA Registry (OM1, Inc.; Boston, MA, USA). Patients with RA (≥ 18 years) treated with upadacitinib or other ATs who previously received a TNFi and had high disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI] > 22) and both a tender joint count and swollen joint count of ≥ 6 at baseline were included. The outcome of interest was achievement of CDAI low disease activity (LDA)/remission at 12 months. Descriptive statistics were reported for proportion of patients who achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months. Multivariable analyses using generalized estimating equation compared CDAI LDA/remission rates for upadacitinib versus IL-6 inhibitors, T cell co-stimulation modulator, and TNFi. A total of 378 patients were included in the analysis: upadacitinib (N = 73), IL-6 inhibitors (N = 64), T cell co-stimulation modulator (N = 76), or a different TNFi (N = 165). Descriptive statistics showed a greater proportion of patients receiving upadacitinib achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months (43.8%) versus IL-6 inhibitors (23.4%), T cell co-stimulation modulator (30.3%), or TNFi (31.5%). Multivariable analyses showed that patients receiving other ATs including IL-6 inhibitors (odds ratio, OR [95% confidence interval] 0.35 [0.16, 0.76], p = 0.01), T cell co-stimulation modulator (OR 0.46 [0.22, 0.95], p = 0.04), or TNFi (OR 0.52 [0.29, 0.96], p = 0.04) had lower odds of achieving CDAI remission/LDA compared to those receiving upadacitinib. In this real-world analysis of patients with RA who previously received TNFis and had high disease burden, more patients treated with upadacitinib achieved CDAI LDA/remission at 12 months versus other ATs.

items.title: A Case of SLE Flare With Class IV Lupus Nephritis and Tuberculous Meningitis Presenting as Neuropsychiatric Symptoms: A Diagnostic Dilemma.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a multisystem autoimmune disease with potential neuropsychiatric involvement (NPSLE) and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections like tuberculosis (TB), particularly in endemic regions such as Nepal where the estimated incidence is 229 per 100,000 population. Differentiating NPSLE from tuberculous meningitis (TBM) is diagnostically challenging due to overlapping clinical and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings. A 25-year-old male with a 1-year history of SLE presented with facial puffiness, oral ulcers, polyarthritis, lower limb edema, and a 6-week history of renal symptoms. Laboratory investigations revealed microcytic anemia (Hb 7.4 g/dL), nephrotic-range proteinuria (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 4.8 g/g), strongly positive anti-dsDNA, and low complement levels. ENA panel was positive for anti-Ro/SSA but negative for antiribosomal P and antiphospholipid antibodies. Renal biopsy confirmed class IV lupus nephritis (Activity Index 11/24 and Chronicity Index 3/12). Following intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy (500 mg/day for 3 days), he developed generalized tonic-clonic seizures and altered sensorium. EEG revealed epileptiform discharges. CSF analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (500 cells/μL and 80% lymphocytes), elevated protein (578 mg/dL), low glucose (1.4 mmol/L), and elevated ADA (10.9 U/L), suggestive of TBM despite negative GeneXpert MTB/RIF, viral PCR, and cryptococcal antigen assays. MRI brain showed cerebral atrophy, calcified granulomas in the right temporal lobe, and a nonspecific demyelinating white matter lesion. Based on clinical, CSF, and imaging findings, empirical antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated alongside tailored immunosuppression. The patient's neurological and renal status markedly improved with complete resolution of seizures. Distinguishing NPSLE from CNS infections requires careful evaluation of serial CSF parameters, biomarkers, and MRI findings. In endemic regions, empirical ATT should be initiated early when clinical and laboratory features suggest TBM, even when molecular or culture tests are negative. In SLE patients with neuropsychiatric symptoms in TB-endemic areas, clinicians must consider TBM even when definitive microbiological tests are negative. Early empirical treatment can significantly improve patient survival and long-term outcomes.

items.title: Paint me a picture: illustrating the psychosocial impact of different juvenile idiopathic arthritis categories.
items.abstract: To describe the impact of different JIA categories on the psychosocial well-being of children and identify associated factors. 1072 patients enrolled in the Canadian Alliance of Pediatric Rheumatology Investigators (CAPRI) registry within three months of diagnosis were included. Psychosocial impact of JIA was measured using the Juvenile Arthritis Quality of Life Questionnaire Psychosocial domain (JAQQ-psychosocial, 1=nil to 7=severe). Wilcoxon ranked-sum tests compared scores at enrollment and one year. Hierarchical clustering of standardized z-scores of JAQQ-psychosocial items produced heatmaps. Spearman correlation and linear regression investigated factors associated with JAQQ-psychosocial scores. At enrollment, median JAQQ-psychosocial was highest for RF+ polyarthritis (3.2, IQR: 1.8-4.4) and lowest for oligoarthritis (1.8, 1-3). Scores improved significantly by one year for RF+ and RF- polyarthritis, psoriatic and systemic arthritis (P < 0.05). JAQQ-psychosocial items clustered into externalizing behaviours, internalizing behaviours, and school-related problems. Heatmaps revealed four clusters with mild (51.0% of patients), moderate (30.6%), severe (9.3%), and very severe (9.1%) JIA psychosocial impact, with the proportions of patients in each cluster varying by JIA category. Most patients improved by 1 year but few patients in each category had persisting or worsening psychosocial impact. Multiple factors correlated with JAQQ-psychosocial scores, and physical disability, fatigue, and pain interference were independently associated with scores at enrollment. JIA psychosocial impact was most severe at diagnosis, varied by JIA category, and improved by 1 year for many children, but few patients showed persisting or worsening JIA impact. Physical disability, fatigue, and pain interference were independently associated with psychosocial impact.

items.title: Identification of C3d Complement Fragments in Lesional Tissues in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis.
items.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is typically described as "pauci-immune" due to the absence or weak detection of Igs and complement activation within AAV tissue lesions. However, complement fragments have been recently reported in significant amounts in damaged tissue in AAV, notably in traps formed by neutrophil extravasation. This study aimed to characterize complement activation, in particular the long-lasting fragment C3d, in affected tissue in AAV. Biopsies from patients with AAV (kidney, n = 40; lung, n = 5; sinus, n = 2; and skin, n = 3), IgA nephropathy (IgAN; kidney, n = 29), C3 glomerulonephritis (C3G; kidney, n = 9), lupus nephritis (LN; kidney, n = 30), and cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis (skin, n = 41) were stained using a novel anti-C3d monoclonal antibody (3d8b), and, in some instances, a commercially available anti-C3c polyclonal antibody. Both semiquantitative scoring and digital quantification revealed moderate glomerular staining in AAV and IgAN and higher signal in C3G and LN. A distinct C3c/C3d glomerular staining pattern was seen in AAV and IgAN with more deposition in mesangium than capillaries. C3G and LN exhibited more homogenous deposition. Three of seven biopsies that tested negative for C3 by routine diagnostic immunostaining were positive for C3d. C3d deposition was also detected in extra-glomerular small vessels in the kidney, in superficial dermal vasculature in leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and in lung and sinus lesional tissues in AAV. Immunostaining for complement fragments, particularly C3d, reveals evidence of complement activation in multiple tissues in AAV, including biopsies deemed negative by routine C3 staining. These data indicate that glomerulonephritis in AAV is less pauci-immune than previously appreciated.

items.title: Implementing Psoriatic Arthritis Screening and Dietary Interventions in Dermatology Practice: A Prospective Clinical Study.
items.abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA) is a common, underdiagnosed inflammatory comorbidity of psoriasis (PsO) that can lead to irreversible joint damage without early intervention. Dermatologists are uniquely positioned to facilitate early PsA detection; however, routine screening remains inconsistent. Lifestyle interventions such as the Mediterranean diet (MD) may further enhance treatment outcomes when combined with biologic therapy. This prospective, single-center, non-randomized controlled study evaluated routine PsA screening and treatment outcomes in an outpatient dermatology clinic. Adults with dermatologist-confirmed PsO were screened for PsA using the Psoriasis Epidemiology Screening Tool (PEST). Patients screening positive self-selected into biologic therapy alone or biologic therapy plus MD intervention. Pain severity was assessed at baseline and 1 month; logistic regression identified predictors of PsA screening positivity, and one-way ANOVA compared pain score changes among treatment groups. a total of 117 PsO patients were screened for PsA; 72 (61.5%) screened positive, representing a statistically significant increase compared with PsA detection prior to implementation of routine PEST screening (P<0.001).Pain severity was the only significant predictor of a positive PsA screen (P<0.001). Both guselkumab- and secukinumab-treated patients were evaluated with and without adherence to the MD; guselkumab combined with the MD demonstrated the greatest reduction in pain scores at 1 month compared with biologic therapy alone (mean change 3.13 ± 1.12; P=0.01). Implementation of routine PsA screening in dermatology practice markedly increased PsA detection. Combining biologic therapy with dietary intervention was associated with greater short-term pain reduction, supporting the utility of lifestyle changes and counseling alongside pharmacologic management in PsA care. &nbsp.

items.title: Bruton Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic relapsing autoimmune disease with frequent cutaneous involvement and unmet treatment need. Given safety and efficacy concerns with first-line therapies and no US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved treatment for cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE), Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) has emerged as a biologically relevant target. On January 20, 2026, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched per PRISMA guidelines. Clinical trials investigating BTK inhibitors for the treatment of SLE were included. Of 579 records, 5 randomized clinical trials met inclusion criteria, evaluating elsubrutinib (2), evobrutinib (1), fenebrutinib (1), and orelabrutinib (1). Efficacy across SLE endpoints was variable. Elsubrutinib- and orelabrutinib-based regimens improved cutaneous disease. Evobrutinib and fenebrutinib showed limited or nonsignificant differences in primary endpoints compared with placebo. Safety was generally acceptable; adverse events included infections and elevations in transaminase levels. BTK inhibitors showed variable efficacy in SLE but potential for cutaneous disease improvement. To date, no clinical trials have evaluated BTK inhibition in CLE. Given promising clinical and mouse model data, dedicated CLE-focused randomized controlled trials are warranted. &nbsp.

items.title: Progression to Psoriatic Arthritis Among Psoriasis Patients Treated With JAK Inhibitors Compared With IL-17/23 Inhibitors.
items.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease that may progress to psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Although multiple systemic therapies are available, including interleukin (IL)-17 and IL-23 inhibitors and Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, their comparative associations with incident PsA remain incompletely characterized. We performed 2 retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort studies within a large federated research network using a TARGET trial emulation framework. Adults with psoriasis initiating a JAK inhibitor were separately compared with those initiating an IL-17 inhibitor or an IL-23 inhibitor; patients with preexisting PsA were excluded. Cohorts were matched 1:1 on demographics, race and ethnicity, comorbidities, psoriasis subtype, baseline musculoskeletal symptoms, prior medication exposure, and healthcare utilization. Balance was assessed using standardized mean differences (<0.10). The primary outcome was incident PsA (L40.5) occurring 1 day to 5 years after treatment initiation. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and time-to-event analyses using Cox models and Kaplan-Meier methods were applied. PsA incidence was 15.1% with IL-23 inhibitors vs 19.0% with JAK inhibitors (RR 1.25, 95% CI 1.15-1.37; HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.20-1.46; log-rank P<0.0001). In contrast, IL-17 inhibitors were associated with a higher incidence than JAK inhibitors (27.1% vs 16.8%; RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.58-0.67; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.61-0.72; log-rank P<0.0001). IL-23 inhibitors were associated with the lowest observed incidence of PsA. Although causal inference is limited, these findings may help inform therapeutic decision-making in psoriasis. &nbsp.

items.title: Mixed Reality-Based Telemedicine for Rheumatoid Arthritis in a Remote Island Setting: A Pilot Feasibility Study (Nagasaki University Rheumatoid Arthritis Remote Medicine System, NURAS).
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) requires regular specialist monitoring; however, access to rheumatologists is severely limited in remote island settings. Conventional two-dimensional video-based telemedicine has limitations for detailed remote joint assessment. This study aimed to evaluate the technical and operational feasibility of the Nagasaki University Rheumatoid Arthritis Remote Medicine System (NURAS), a mixed reality (MR)-based telemedicine platform, for collaborative RA assessment in a remote island setting and to descriptively explore 12-month changes in clinical and patient-reported outcomes. NURAS enables remote rheumatologists to view three-dimensional holographic joint images beyond conventional video telemedicine. In this 12-month single-center pilot feasibility study at Goto Chuoh Hospital, 6 patients with RA were enrolled. An on-site primary care physician and a remote rheumatologist at Nagasaki University Hospital jointly assessed patients at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months using a 28-joint count with real-time MR visualization. Primary outcomes were feasibility metrics, including the numbers of planned, attempted, completed, failed, and rescheduled sessions, connection interruptions, setup and consultation times, technical problems, and completion of planned joint assessments. Secondary outcomes were exploratory changes in disease activity (DAS28-CRP and Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI]) and patient-reported outcomes (HAQ-DI, RAID, FACIT-F, pain visual analogue scale [VAS], and K6), summarized as medians with IQRs. All 18 planned telemedicine sessions were attempted and completed; 2 sessions were rescheduled for patient-related reasons, and no connection interruptions were documented. All planned joint assessments were completed, and setup required approximately 5 minutes per session with assistance from 1 nurse. Median consultation time was 37 minutes 45 seconds at baseline and 17 minutes 46 seconds at 12 months. Median DAS28-CRP decreased from 2.98 to 1.69 and median CDAI from 10.0 to 3.0, whereas patient-reported outcomes varied across individuals. Clinical outcome changes were interpreted descriptively. NURAS was technically and operationally feasible for collaborative, specialist-supported RA care in a remote island setting. Larger controlled studies are needed to evaluate diagnostic agreement, acceptability, technical performance, cost, and clinical effectiveness. This study was a noninterventional observational feasibility study and was not prospectively registered. The study was approved by the Nagasaki University Hospital Clinical Research Ethics Committee (approval number: 21081605).

items.title: TAK1 signaling in fibrosis: insights from systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a complex autoimmune disease characterized by fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, vascular abnormalities, and immune dysregulation. Widespread and recalcitrant fibrosis underlies the significant morbidity and mortality of SSc. TGF-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), a key regulator of various cellular processes including inflammation and fibrosis has emerged as a pivotal player in the pathogenesis of fibrotic diseases such as SSc. This timely review explores the biology and multifaceted roles of TAK1 in SSc, encompassing its involvement in fibroblast activation, immune cell function, and endothelial dysfunction. Mechanistically, TAK1 integrates signals from diverse cytokines and growth factors to modulate downstream effectors such as NF-κB and MAP kinases, thereby influencing inflammation, oxidative stress, and tissue remodeling in SSc. Notably, dysregulation of TAK1 signaling pathways has been implicated in the aberrant activation of fibroblasts and the persistence of profibrotic responses characteristic of SSc. Understanding the intricate network of TAK1-mediated intracellular signaling pathways offers new insights into potential therapeutic strategies targeting this kinase for the treatment of SSc and fibrosis. This review synthesizes current knowledge and highlights promising avenues for future research aimed at harnessing TAK1 as a therapeutic target in SSc management.

items.title: Recurrent hypofibrinogenemia after reduced-dose tocilizumab rechallenge in rheumatoid arthritis: a case report.
items.abstract: Tocilizumab (TCZ), a monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-6 receptor, is widely used for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other inflammatory diseases. Reductions in fibrinogen levels have been reported during TCZ treatment, and some patients develop hypofibrinogenemia. Clinical experience with TCZ re-exposure after such an event, particularly at a reduced dose, remains limited. We report a 76-year-old woman with RA whose disease remained inadequately controlled despite multiple antirheumatic therapies. On 24 April 2026, intravenous TCZ was reinitiated at 400 mg, with a pretreatment fibrinogen level of 3.29 g/L. Approximately 1 month later, fibrinogen had fallen to 0.85 g/L without clinically apparent bleeding. Further TCZ treatment was withheld, and 20 units of cryoprecipitate were administered. Fibrinogen initially increased to 1.99 g/L and subsequently returned to 2.07 g/L during the period without further TCZ exposure. Her RA subsequently became highly active again and remained inadequately controlled despite ongoing conventional antirheumatic treatment. After discussion of the previous adverse event and the potential risks of re-exposure, TCZ was restarted on 19 July 2026, at a reduced intravenous dose of 240 mg; the most recent fibrinogen level before re-exposure was 2.07 g/L. Her joint symptoms and inflammatory markers improved, but 17 days later fibrinogen again decreased to 1.05 g/L, without clinically evident bleeding. The temporal association with TCZ reinitiation in 2026, subsequent recovery during TCZ withdrawal, and recurrence after reduced-dose rechallenge support a probable association between TCZ and hypofibrinogenemia in this patient. This case shows that hypofibrinogenemia can recur despite substantial TCZ dose reduction in a patient with a previous TCZ-associated episode. If TCZ re-exposure is considered clinically necessary, closer monitoring of fibrinogen may be warranted.

items.title: Molecular endotyping in systemic lupus erythematosus: an integrative framework toward precision therapy.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a clinically defined syndrome arising from heterogeneous and dynamically interacting molecular programs. Recent transcriptomic, single-cell, spatial, and functional studies have identified recurrent molecular states; however, published three-, five-, six-, and eight-group taxonomies are not directly interchangeable. In this review, the published evidence was synthesized within a pragmatic framework of four overlapping candidate programs: interferon/interferon-stimulated gene (IFN/ISG), B cell/plasmablast, neutrophil/neutrophil extracellular trap (NET), and an emerging immunometabolic program. Complement/immune-complex activation is considered a cross-cutting effector axis rather than a mutually exclusive endotype. The molecular endotype is defined operationally, and a distinction is made between pathway signatures, candidate endotypes, and clinically actionable endotypes. In this review, activity biomarkers, prognostic biomarkers, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and predictive biomarkers are distinguished; the transcriptomic ISG-high states are distinguished from directly measurable type I IFN bioactivity; and the contributions of short-lived plasmablasts and long-lived plasma cells to autoantibody production are also examined. It should be emphasized that endotype assignment is time- and compartment-dependent and that blood signatures may not fully capture organ-specific disease, particularly lupus nephritis. Molecular endotyping in SLE should therefore be viewed as a research framework toward precision therapy rather than as a current treatment algorithm. Prospective biomarker-enriched trials and longitudinal multi-compartment profiling will be required to establish clinically actionable endotypes.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based decision support for axial spondyloarthritis integrating inflammatory and structural MRI information.
items.abstract: Axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) assessment on MRI is complicated by interpretation difficulty and by clinical variables that may be incomplete at the time of imaging. We aimed to develop an image-only deep learning framework to approximate the clinical assessment of axSpA from sacroiliac joint (SIJ) MRI, integrating fat-suppressed T1-weighted (FS T1) and short tau inversion recovery (STIR) sequences to capture structural and inflammatory information without clinical variables. This retrospective study included patients with chronic back pain who underwent SIJ MRI from January 2010 to December 2021. The treating rheumatologist's clinical diagnosis served as the reference standard. A two-stage framework integrated FS T1 and STIR features with Stage 1-derived binary bone marrow edema (BME) predictions to generate an axSpA probability. Performance in a test set was compared with the Assessment of SpondyloArthritis International Society (ASAS) definition of a "positive MRI" and the ASAS classification criteria using exact McNemar tests; discordant cases were analyzed separately. Among 291 patients (163 axSpA, 128 non-axSpA), the model achieved an AUROC of 0.9412, accuracy of 86.0%, sensitivity of 87.5%, and specificity of 84.0% in the test set (n=57). No significant paired differences in accuracy, sensitivity, or specificity were detected between the model and either ASAS comparator. In an exploratory analysis of 10 cases discordant between ASAS "positive MRI" assessment and clinical diagnosis, the model correctly classified 7 (70.0%). The model showed similar performance to the ASAS-based comparators in the test set without clinical variables, suggesting potential value as an image-based decision-support tool. External multicenter validation is needed to confirm generalizability.

items.title: Case Report: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis presenting as a multiple sclerosis mimic.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) rarely involves the central nervous system and may closely resemble inflammatory demyelinating disease. We report a 32-year-old woman with adult-onset asthma and recurrent sinusitis who presented with bilateral lower-extremity sensory symptoms and neuropathic pain. Brain and spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multifocal T2-hyperintense lesions fulfilling dissemination in space and time according to the 2017 McDonald criteria. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed mild pleocytosis, CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands, and eosinophils on qualitative cytological examination. Multiple sclerosis (MS) was initially suspected and intravenous methylprednisolone resulted in partial improvement. Three weeks later, the patient developed palpable purpura, inflammatory arthralgia, and left foot-elevating paresis. Follow-up MRI demonstrated a new enhancing lesion and electrophysiological studies revealed axonal neuropathy. Retrospective review of the initial laboratory results showed that peripheral eosinophilia was already present at baseline, while subsequent evaluation identified eosinophilic gastritis on gastroscopic biopsy and eosinophilic bone marrow infiltration. The diagnosis of EGPA was established based on the clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and histopathological evidence of eosinophilic inflammation, and the patient fulfilled the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for EGPA. Treatment with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide followed by maintenance mepolizumab resulted in sustained clinical stability. This case highlights that EGPA may present with radiological and CSF-findings suggestive of MS and emphasizes the importance of integrating systemic manifestations to avoid diagnostic delay.

items.title: Pretreatment neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is associated with clinical phenotypes and infection-related mortality in microscopic polyangiitis: the multicentre REVEAL cohort study.
items.abstract: Microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in immunosuppressive therapy, highlighting the need for simple biomarkers that facilitate LR) has been associated with disease activity and prognosis in antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV), its phenotype-specific significance in newly diagnosed MPA remains unclear. We investigated whether pretreatment NLR is associated with clinical phenotype, disease course, and long-term outcomes in MPA. Among 418 patients with MPA enrolled in the multicentre REVEAL cohort between 2005 and 2025, 340 newly diagnosed treatment-naïve patients fulfilling the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria were included. Patients were stratified into tertiles according to pretreatment NLR. Baseline characteristics, temporal outcomes, and survival were compared. Infection-related mortality was further evaluated after stabilised inverse probability weighting (IPW). Higher pretreatment NLR was associated with greater disease severity, including higher Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score ( P  < 0.001) and Five-Factor Score ( P  = 0.03), more frequent diffuse alveolar haemorrhage ( P  = 0.015), poorer renal function ( P  = 0.003), and more intensive remission-induction therapy, including methylprednisolone pulse therapy and rituximab. In contrast, interstitial lung disease was more common in patients with lower NLR ( P  = 0.001). Despite these baseline differences, disease activity, glucocorticoid tapering, and cumulative organ damage became comparable after treatment initiation. Pretreatment NLR was not associated with relapse-free survival ( P  = 0.44) but was associated with poorer overall survival ( P  = 0.012) and higher infection-related mortality ( P  = 0.002). After adjustment using IPW, the association with overall survival was no longer statistically significant, whereas the increased risk of infection-related mortality remained significant (HR 3.47, 95% CI 1.32-9.09, P  = 0.034). Pretreatment NLR reflected distinct inflammatory phenotypes and was independently associated with infection-related mortality in patients with newly diagnosed MPA. As an inexpensive and widely available marker, pretreatment NLR may have potential as a prognostic biomarker, although further validation is required to establish its clinical utility.

items.title: Deciphering the microbiota-immune axis in adult-onset Still's disease: evidence from Mendelian randomization and experimental evaluation.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a systemic autoinflammatory disorder with unclear etiology. Although gut microbiota may influence immune-mediated diseases, their genetically predicted associations with AOSD remain unclear. This study aims to investigate the potential associations between gut microbiota and AOSD susceptibility and to elucidate the potential mediating roles of immune-cell traits. A two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) framework was employed using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the Dutch Microbiome Project (7,738 individuals), FinnGen cohort (113 AOSD cases and 341,455 controls), and 731 immune-cell traits (3,757 individuals). Potential associations with AOSD susceptibility were assessed using inverse-variance weighted (IVW) and Bayesian weighted MR (BWMR) methods, with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and were complemented by comprehensive sensitivity analyses to assess robustness. A two-step MR approach was subsequently applied to investigate potential immune-mediated effects. The inflammatory potential of the identified microbial taxa was further examined in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice and microbiota-depleted models treated with Parabacteroides goldsteinii ( P. goldsteinii ) and Alistipes shahii ( A. shahii ). MR analysis identified 10 microbial taxa and three metabolic pathways significantly associated with AOSD susceptibility. Notably, the taxa Streptococcaceae, Streptococcus , P. goldsteinii , Parabacteroides distasonis , and A. shahii showed positive genetically predicted associations with increased risks of AOSD, whereas Verrucomicrobia and Akkermansia exhibited inverse associations. Mediation analysis revealed that several T-cell-related immune traits, including CD127 + CD4 + T cells and CD25 hi CD4 + T cells, partially mediated these associations, with mediation proportions ranging from 3.44% to 26.79%. Importantly, administration of P. goldsteinii and A. shahii significantly increased circulating levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in CIA mice, supporting the biological plausibility of the MR findings. This study integrates genetic and experimental evidence to support potential roles of gut microbiota in AOSD susceptibility and immune dysregulation. Specific taxa, including P. goldsteinii and A. shahii , may exhibit pro-inflammatory effects, while Akkermansia may have protective effects. These findings offer novel insights into microbiota-immune interactions in AOSD, and highlight potential microbial and immunological targets for future therapeutic intervention.

items.title: Association between Blood Biomarkers and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity: A Retrospective Study from Indonesia.
items.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease, and laboratory parameters are essential for monitoring disease activity. To determine the association between blood biomarkers and SLE disease activity in an Indonesian tertiary hospital. This retrospective study included adult patients with SLE treated at a tertiary hospital in Indonesia between January 2022 and August 2024. Patients were categorized into mild (inactive) or moderate-severe (active) disease activity groups, based on the MEX-SLEDAI score. Demographic and laboratory variables were collected. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was done to assess discriminatory performance. Multivariate logistic regression was conducted to identify independent indicators of moderate-severe disease activity. A total of 110 patients were included: 52 with active and 58 with inactive SLE. Between the groups, patients with active SLE had significantly lower hemoglobin ( P < 0.001), hematocrit ( P < 0.001), and platelet count ( P = 0.019). In addition, significant differences were found for differential leukocyte counts and inflammatory hematological parameters, except the systemic immune-inflammation response index. ROC analysis showed that neutrophil percentage and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio had the highest discriminatory performance (for both, AUC = 0.819), with optimal cut-offs of >68% (sensitivity: 67.3%; specificity: 87.9%) and >2.83 (sensitivity: 75.0%; specificity: 84.5%), respectively. In multivariate logistic regression, platelet count ( P = 0.048) and eosinophil percentage ( P = 0.026) were found to be independently associated with moderate-severe SLE activity. This study found that low platelet count and eosinopenia were independently associated with moderate-severe SLE disease activity, while neutrophil percentage and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio demonstrated good discriminatory performance for distinguishing between active and inactive SLE.

items.title: Technical refinement of semispinalis cervicis-preserving occipitocervical fixation for rheumatoid arthritis/basilar invagination.
items.abstract: Conventional occipitocervical (O-C) fixation for rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-associated basilar invagination (BI) may require extensive dissection and detachment of the posterior cervical extensor musculature. As this included the semispinalis cervicis (SSC), it may result in significant postoperative axial neck pain. Here, we describe a technical refinement of O-C fixation that preserves the SSC distal to its C2 attachment. A 48-year-old female presented with RA-associated BI and C4/5 spondylolisthesis. A posterior O-C to C5 fixation utilized an intermuscular dissection plane between the SSC and semispinalis capitis. Utilizing 3-D navigation, this allowed for exposure of the subaxial screw entry points while preserving the SSC caudal to C2, and ensured accurate screw placement. Postoperatively, at 8 postoperative months, her axial neck pain improved (i.e., visual analog scale 6-1), bridging bone indicated solid fusion, while the magnetic resonance confirmed indirect adequate neural decompression without SSC atrophy. This SSC-preserving O-C-C5 fixation technique achieved successful fusion in this case while avoiding postoperative axial neck pain and SSC atrophy.

items.title: [Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: a disease easily underestimated by rhinologists].
items.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis commonly presents with asthma and chronic rhinosinusitis with or without nasal polyps as early hallmark manifestations. Owing to its rarity, EGPA remains underrecognized in clinical practice, leading to substantial diagnostic challenges and delayed diagnosis. This review systematically summarizes the epidemiology, immunopathological mechanisms, and recent advances in the diagnosis and management of EGPA, with a particular focus on sinonasal involvement. This review highlights the pivotal role of rhinologists in identifying early warning signs and implementing appropriate diagnostic pathways. By adopting a rhinology-oriented perspective, this review aims to facilitate earlier recognition of EGPA, reduce diagnostic delay, and ultimately improve patient prognosis and long-term outcomes. 摘要: 嗜酸性肉芽肿性多血管炎（eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis，EGPA）常以哮喘、慢性鼻窦炎伴或不伴鼻息肉作为特征性初始表现。由于EGPA临床罕见，目前公众乃至部分临床医师对该病认知不足，导致早期诊断识别面临严重挑战。本文系统综述EGPA的流行病学特征、免疫病理机制及诊疗进展，重点解析其鼻腔鼻窦病变特征，强调鼻科医生在预警信号识别和诊断路径实施中的关键作用，旨在建立基于鼻科视角的早期诊疗策略，以期实现疾病的早期识别，避免诊断延误，最终改善患者的预后和长期结局。.

items.title: Serum IgG N-glycosylation profiles distinguish primary Sjögren's disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic lupus erythematosus and are associated with disease activity in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: IgG N-glycosylation regulates immune effector functions and inflammation, but disease-specific patterns in primary Sjögren's disease (SjD), rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are insufficiently defined, particularly in SjD. To identify serum IgG N-glycan biomarkers that differentiate SjD, RA, and SLE and reflect disease activity in SjD. A clinical case-control study. Serum IgG N-glycans from 88 SjD patients, 102 RA patients, 86 SLE patients and 91 healthy controls were profiled using ultra-performance liquid chromatography. Discriminative glycans were selected through machine learning-based feature selection and evaluated for their diagnostic performance using cross-validated logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. All three diseases exhibited decreased galactosylation and increased bisecting N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc). SjD showed the lowest sialylation (19.92%) and the highest bisecting GlcNAc levels (19.36%). Shared features included elevated GP1 (FA1) and reduced GP9 (FA2[3]G1). Compared with RA, SjD was characterized by elevated GP3 (A2B, adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 4.27), GP8 (FA2[6]G1, AOR 3.53) and reduced GP23 (FA2G2S2, AOR 0.07). Elevated GP11 (FA2[3]BG1, AOR 11.99) distinguished SjD from SLE. These glycans outperformed conventional autoantibodies in ROC analysis. In SjD, higher disease activity was associated with reduced galactosylation, with GP5 (M5) positively (AOR 1.71) and GP14 (FA2G2) inversely (AOR 0.43) associated with activity. These glycans showed stronger correlations with disease activity than erythrocyte sedimentation rate or serum IgG levels (GP5: r = 0.462; GP14: r = -0.432), and the combined glycan model achieved an AUC of 0.758. Distinct IgG N-glycan signatures differentiate SjD, RA, and SLE despite their shared clinical and immunologic characteristics and are associated with disease activity in SjD. These findings provide insights into IgG N-glycosylation in these autoimmune diseases and may inform future research into their potential utility as non-invasive biomarkers, particularly in SjD. The immune system produces antibodies to help protect the body from infections. Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is the most abundant antibody in the blood and has small sugar structures attached to it. These sugars influence how the immune system functions and regulate inflammation. Changes in these sugar structures have been reported in several autoimmune diseases. However, it has remained unclear whether different autoimmune diseases have distinct IgG sugar patterns, particularly in primary Sjögren’s disease (SjD), an autoimmune disease that mainly affects the salivary and tear glands. In this study, we analyzed blood samples from people with SjD, rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and healthy individuals. We examined the sugar patterns attached to IgG to determine whether they could help distinguish these diseases and whether they were associated with disease activity in SjD. Using advanced laboratory techniques and statistical analyses, we identified the IgG sugar patterns that best distinguished the disease groups. We found that all three autoimmune diseases showed IgG sugar changes associated with increased inflammatory activity. However, patients with SjD showed the most pronounced changes and distinct sugar patterns that helped distinguish SjD from RA and SLE. These IgG sugar markers also showed better discriminatory performance than commonly used blood tests. In addition, several IgG sugar changes were associated with disease activity in SjD and showed stronger associations than conventional inflammatory markers. Overall, our findings suggest that IgG sugar patterns may serve as useful blood-based biomarkers to help distinguish SjD from related autoimmune diseases and to assess disease activity. These findings support further investigation of IgG sugar patterns as potential non-invasive biomarkers in autoimmune diseases.

items.title: Comparative Ethnopharmacological Insights Into Anti-Inflammatory Phytochemicals From Indian and Chinese Medicinal Plants in the Management of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by synovial inflammation, pain and progressive joint damage. The traditional medicines of India and China have used herbal remedies for the treatment of inflammatory diseases for centuries. The ethnopharmacological history of such medicines is an asset that can be explored for the use of herbal remedies in RA. The present study reviews medicinal plants of Indian and Chinese origin, emphasizing phytochemicals with demonstrated anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidant and immunomodulatory activities relevant to rheumatoid arthritis. A narrative literature review was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar databases up to 2025. Literature that described the isolation, characterization, and biological evaluation of active compounds from traditional medicinal plants was taken into account. Phytoconstituents such as flavonoids, terpenoids, saponins, alkaloids and polyphenols exhibit inhibition of pro-inflammatory mediators including TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, COX-2 and NF-κB. Several plants like Curcuma longa, Boswellia serrata, Zingiber officinale and Camellia sinensis demonstrate potential anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties, which make them beneficial in treating arthritis. Medicinal plants from Indian and Chinese systems offer potential as supportive agents in RA management. Additional research should concentrate on the aspects of standardization, mechanistic studies and clinical validation to confirm their therapeutic benefits and their safe use alongside other traditional therapies.

items.title: KneeMS to Monitor Knee Acoustic Emissions for Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
items.abstract: Wearable sensing for capturing knee acoustic emissions (KAEs) can enable earlier detection and better management of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA). In this paper, we expand on our previous work by validating the KneeMS wearable for individuals with JIA in a clinical setting against a benchtop system (Dytran). Acoustic features were recorded from the medial and lateral sides of the patellar tendon using both Dytran and KneeMS in 36 participants with JIA during flexion/extension (FE). We calculated the Spearman correlation coefficient ( ρ ) between the acoustic features of both devices Acoustic features were recorded from the medial and lateral sides of the patellar tendon using both Dytran and KneeMS in 36 participants with JIA during flexion/extension (FE). We calculated the Spearman correlation coefficient between the acoustic features of both devices and assessed severity trends and longitudinal tracking of JIA knees from a machine learning (ML) pipeline differentiating active from inactive JIA knees. Of 36 extracted features, six had the highest ρ (medial/lateral): RMS (0.79/0.70), MFCC1 (0.79/0.72), spectral slope (0.78/0.68), energy (0.78/0.67), Hjorth activity (0.75/0.71), and spectral flux (0.74/0.69). Our ML pipeline demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) mean of 0.77 ( p< 0.05 ) and showed a significant ( p< 0.05 ) upward trend in active knee prediction probabilities P(A) with clinical severity using KneeMS. For follow-ups, KneeMS P(A) moved in the clinically expected direction for 4 of 5 status-changing knees (versus 1 of 5 for Dytran); the clinical JADAS (cJADAS) score, available for most knees, was consistent with this finding. The high correlation between the acoustic features of Dytran and KneeMS, a significant AUC-ROC, significant JIA severity trend, and prospective longitudinal tracking make KneeMS a viable alternative to Dytran. This validation establishes the foundation of home-based longitudinal joint assessment for JIA.Clinical and Translational Impact Statement: Wearable acoustic monitoring could enable at-home tracking of JIA disease activity, supporting timely treatment.

items.title: Evaluation of renal parenchymal stiffness using shear wave elastography in Behçet's disease without clinical renal involvement.
items.abstract: Renal involvement in Behçet's disease is uncommon but clinically relevant and may remain subclinical in the absence of abnormal renal function tests or urinalysis findings. Shear wave elastography (SWE) may provide quantitative information on renal parenchymal stiffness beyond conventional ultrasonographic parameters. To evaluate renal parenchymal stiffness using SWE in patients with Behçet's disease without clinical, biochemical, or urinalysis evidence of renal involvement. This prospective case-control study included 29 patients with Behçet's disease and 40 healthy controls. All participants underwent conventional renal ultrasonography and renal SWE using a standardized protocol. Renal length, width, cortical thickness, and right and left renal parenchymal stiffness values were recorded. Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, disease activity scores, organ involvement, and treatment status were analyzed in the Behçet's disease group. Patients with Behçet's disease had significantly higher right, left, and mean renal parenchymal stiffness values than healthy controls. Mean renal stiffness was 6.87 ± 1.39 kPa in the Behçet's disease group and 4.87 ± 0.39 kPa in controls (p < 0.001). In contrast, renal length, width, and cortical thickness did not differ significantly between groups. Mean renal stiffness showed a positive correlation with erythrocyte sedimentation rate (r = 0.675, p < 0.001). In multivariable linear regression analysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate remained independently associated with mean renal stiffness, while composite immunosuppressive treatment was associated with lower stiffness values. Exploratory ROC analysis showed good discriminatory performance of mean renal stiffness for differentiating patients with Behçet's disease from controls. Renal parenchymal stiffness is increased in patients with Behçet's disease despite normal renal function, normal urinalysis, and preserved conventional ultrasonographic parameters. As a pilot study, these findings suggest that SWE may provide additional quantitative information on subclinical renal parenchymal alterations in Behçet's disease; however, larger longitudinal studies are required to validate its clinical significance.

items.title: A Rare Presentation of Lupus Nephritis: Postpartum Complement-Mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome Mimicking Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura.
items.abstract: Complement-mediated hemolytic uremic syndrome (CM-HUS) is a rare form of thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may complicate systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and can be difficult to distinguish from thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), because both present with thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and end-organ injury. We report a 21-year-old woman with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, hypertriglyceridemia, and a positive antinuclear antibody who presented four months postpartum with nausea, vomiting, headache, and facial swelling. Evaluation revealed severe hypertension, anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, nephrotic-range proteinuria, and hematuria, and a peripheral smear showed schistocytes consistent with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. Given concern for TTP, she underwent therapeutic plasma exchange and received high-dose corticosteroids with initial improvement. Further workup demonstrated markedly elevated anti-double-stranded DNA antibodies, profound hypocomplementemia, and biopsy-proven Class III lupus nephritis with thrombotic microangiopathy, while ADAMTS13 activity was preserved at 94%, effectively excluding TTP and supporting lupus-associated CM-HUS. Plasma exchange was discontinued and the patient was treated with hydroxychloroquine, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, and corticosteroids; complement inhibition with eculizumab was deferred given an ongoing response. At follow-up, platelet count and renal function normalized and hemoglobin stabilized on immunosuppression alone. Pregnancy and the postpartum period are recognized complement-amplifying states that may precipitate endothelial injury and unmask autoimmune disease. This case underscores that preserved ADAMTS13 activity, active lupus serologies, hypocomplementemia, and biopsy-proven lupus nephritis are critical to distinguishing CM-HUS from TTP and to guiding lupus-directed therapy that can achieve favorable hematologic and renal recovery.

items.title: Research Advances in Targeted Modulation of Macrophage M1/M2 Polarization for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a disease of the immune system that leads to continuous synovial inflammation and the progressive breakdown of joints. As essential effector cells in innate immunity, macrophages can become either pro-inflammatory M1 or anti-inflammatory M2 phenotypes, playing a critical role in RA pathogenesis. A marked M1/M2 polarization imbalance exists in the synovial microenvironment of RA, in which excessive activation and accumulation of M1 macrophages serve as a key hub driving persistent inflammation, cartilage degradation, and bone erosion. Currently, conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) with methotrexate (MTX) as the anchor agent remain the mainstay for RA management; however, approximately 30%-40% of RA patients show an inadequate response to MTX, resulting in persistent synovial inflammation, progressive joint damage, and difficult-to-control disease. For macrophage-directed phenotypic modulation in RA therapy, novel smart nanodelivery systems are a key research focus, while accumulating preclinical evidence supports the capacity of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) to restore M1/M2 homeostasis. This review systematically summarizes the polarization mechanisms of macrophages in RA, their core pathological functions, and recent advances in targeting these cells as therapeutic strategies, therefore delivering novel insights and references for RA treatment through targeted changes in macrophage polarization.

items.title: Mapping mortality predictors and prognostic models in anti-MDA5 dermatomyositis-associated RP-ILD: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (anti-MDA5) dermatomyositis is associated with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD) and high early mortality. Accurate prognostication is critical, but existing literature is heterogeneous. This scoping review aims to map reported risk factors for mortality and evaluate existing prognostic models in anti-MDA5-associated RP-ILD (anti-MDA5 + RP-ILD). A PRISMA-ScR-adherent systematic search of PubMed and Embase was conducted from inception until 16/07/2025, and subsequently updated from 17/07/2025 to 02/10/2026. Eligible observational studies evaluated mortality-associated factors in anti-MDA5-positive RP-ILD or prognostic models relevant to mortality or RP-ILD development in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis. Systematic reviews, non-empirical studies, grey literature, case reports, and abstracts were excluded. Data extracted included study characteristics, mortality rates, statistically significant prognostic factors, and details of proposed prognostic models. Of 50 studies included (with 44 cohorts), pertinent mortality predictors were identified based on frequency of statistically significant associations. Older age, elevated LDH and ferritin, and hypoalbuminemia were among the factors most frequently reported to be significantly associated with mortality. Of 13 prognostic models identified, 8 predicted mortality in anti-MDA5-positive patients, 2 predicted the development of RP-ILD, and 3 addressed mortality in broader inflammatory myopathy-associated ILD populations. Most were derived from single-centre cohorts. Reported discriminatory performance varied across models, although direct comparisons were limited by heterogeneity in study populations, validation strategies, and performance metrics. Future priorities should include prospective multi-centre validation, standardised disease definitions, dynamic biomarker-based risk assessment, and head-to-head comparison of prognostic models to inform reliable and robust risk stratification and tailored management of anti-MDA5 + RP-ILD. Key Points • This scoping review synthesised evidence from 50 studies, identifying older age, elevated ferritin and lactate dehydrogenase, and hypoalbuminaemia as frequently reported mortality-associated factors in anti-MDA5-associated rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease. • Thirteen prognostic models were identifi ed, diff ering in their target populations, predicted outcomes, constituent variables and validation strategies, limiting direct comparisons and clinical applicability. • Future research should prioritise prospective multicentre validation, standardised outcome definitions and direct comparisons of prognostic models to improve risk stratification in anti-MDA5-associated interstitial lung disease.

items.title: Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase drives fibroblast activation and skin fibrosis in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is characterised by persistent fibroblast activation and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. The mechanisms sustaining profibrotic fibroblast states remain poorly understood. Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), a S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-consuming enzyme that modulates cellular methylation potential, has been implicated in fibrotic tissue remodelling. In this study, we investigated the role of NNMT in dermal fibroblast (DF) activation and fibrosis in SSc. Bulk RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq), single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics datasets from SSc skin were analysed. Primary human DFs were subjected to small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated NNMT knockdown or pharmacological NNMT inhibition followed by transcriptomic, metabolomic, epigenetic, and functional profiling. Downstream transcription factors were assessed by QuantSeq 3' RNA-Seq following activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), SRY-box transcription factor (SOX9), and serum response factor (SRF) knockdown. Pharmacological NNMT inhibition was evaluated in bleomycin-induced dermal fibrosis. NNMT was upregulated in SSc skin across independent cohorts and enriched in disease-expanded myofibroblast states. NNMT knockdown altered the SAM/S-adenosylhomocysteine ratio and histone methylation patterns, and attenuated transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ)-induced profibrotic programs associated with ECM production, collagen synthesis and tissue remodelling. Mechanistically, NNMT supported TGFβ-induced activation of an ATF4/SOX9/SRF transcriptional network that contributed to ECM gene expression and collagen secretion. Pharmacological NNMT inhibition recapitulated key effects of NNMT depletion, suppressed disease-associated SSc fibroblast programs, and attenuated experimental dermal fibrosis in vivo. These findings identify a TGFβ-NNMT-ATF4/SOX9/SRF regulatory network linking metabolic regulation to DF activation. Targeting NNMT may represent a therapeutic strategy to attenuate fibrosis in SSc.

items.title: Huashi Runzao Decoction alleviates ferroptosis in salivary gland epithelial cells through RBM15B-associated m 6 A regulation in Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Huashi Runzao Decoction (HSRZD) is a well established herbal formula developed for the clinical management of Sjögren's disease (SjD). Previous randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that HSRZD improves salivary gland function and reduces disease activity in patients with SjD. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of HSRZD against salivary gland dysfunction in Sjögren's disease (SjD) and to explore the mechanisms underlying m 6 A mediated regulation of salivary gland injury. The chemical profile of HSRZD was characterized by UHPLC-MS/MS. NOD/ShiLtJ mice and IFN-γ-stimulated primary human salivary gland epithelial cells (SGECs) were used to evaluate the protective effects of HSRZD against SjD associated salivary gland dysfunction and ferroptotic injury. Dysregulated m 6 A regulators were screened and identified as potential mediators involved in SjD pathogenesis and HSRZD treatment. RNA-seq, gene silencing, RIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, and MeRIP-qPCR were performed to elucidate the role of the RBM15B mediated m 6 A regulatory pathway in regulating GPX4 mRNA stability and ferroptosis in SGECs. A total of 118 chemical constituents were identified in the HSRZD aqueous decoction. In NOD/ShiLtJ mice, HSRZD improved salivary gland function, suppressed ferroptosis in SMG tissues, and restored RBM15B expression, while RBM15B was markedly downregulated in primary SGECs from patients with SjD. RBM15B silencing promoted ferroptosis in SGECs and altered the expression of ferroptosis-related genes, with GPX4 showing the most pronounced reduction. RBM15B silencing decreased GPX4 expression and reduced its mRNA stability. Furthermore, RBM15B silencing reduced m 6 A enrichment within the GPX4 mRNA region containing the predicted m 6 A motif at nucleotide 727. In IFN-γ-stimulated SGECs, HSRZD attenuated ferroptosis and restored RBM15B and GPX4 expression, whereas these protective effects were partially abolished by RBM15B silencing. HSRZD alleviates salivary gland dysfunction in SjD by restoring RBM15B expression and enhancing GPX4 mediated ferroptosis resistance in SGECs. The RBM15B-GPX4 axis may represent an m 6 A associated mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of HSRZD in SjD. However, the interactions between HSRZD constituents and RBM15B, and the functional role of the candidate GPX4 m 6 A site, require further experimental validation.

items.title: Kidney Endpoints in ANCA-Associated Vasculitis - Position Report from the European Vasculitis Society Focus Group Meetings.
items.abstract: Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) often affect the kidneys, driving morbidity and mortality in AAV. Clinical trials have investigated kidney outcomes using a variety of definitions. The standardization of kidney disease response criteria in AAV remains an unmet need, with an urgency to define kidney endpoints for daily clinical practice and new drug development to optimize patient management. A European Vasculitis Society (EUVAS) Focus Group was formed to review the literature and discuss the wide range of definitions used. The group involved nephrologists, pathologists and rheumatologists who met four times over a time frame of two years with the objective of formulating a consensus proposal for standardized kidney endpoint definitions for AAV. The group investigated the terminology and outcome relations of active kidney disease, treatment response and refractory kidney disease, remission and relapse, kidney function recovery and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. The group reviewed and discussed measurable parameters used for the assessments, such as kidney biopsy, hematuria and proteinuria, serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate and novel biomarkers. Here, we report on the current variability in terminology, present an expert proposal for kidney endpoints with a research agenda and outline the future strategy for a Delphi consensus.

items.title: Structural and immunological dissection of an anti-C1q autoantibody epitope in systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Autoantibodies targeting C1q (anti-C1q), the recognition protein of the classical complement pathway, are strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). C1q forms a bouquet-shaped octadecamer composed of six heterotrimeric triple helices ((ABC) 6 ), generating collagen-like regions (CLR) and globular head domains. Anti-C1q predominantly target the CLR, including the epitopes A09 and A15 of C1q's A chain. Here, we investigated the structural and immunological relevance of the arginine-rich A09/A15 overlap using CLR_NC2, a headless C1q construct. CLR_NC2 variants were generated by deletion mutagenesis or alanine substitution at positions R16, R19, R20, and R22. Structural characteristics were assessed by mass photometry, differential scanning fluorimetry, LC/ESI-MS, surface plasmon resonance, and electron microscopy, while anti-C1q reactivity was evaluated using plasma from SLE patients (n = 76) and healthy controls (n = 39). Deletion of the A09/A15 overlap or alanine substitution of R19 resulted in low-molecular-weight assemblies, whereas substitutions at R16, R20, and R22 maintained the bouquet-shaped architecture and retained binding to the C1r(SA) 2 C1s(SA) 2 tetramer and the receptor LAIR-1. Immunologically, R20A and R16A-R20A-R22A showed the strongest reduction in anti-C1q binding within SLE plasma. In exploratory clinical analyses, this reduction was most pronounced in patients with high anti-C1q titers, with non-significant trends towards shorter disease duration and hypocomplementaemia at sampling. R19 of C1q's A chain appears to contribute to CLR higher-order assembly, whereas R16, R20, and R22 have minor structural roles but display altered recognition in SLE, with R20 showing a prominent contribution to autoantibody recognition of the A09/A15 region.

items.title: Effect of ethnicity on response to treatment escalation in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR): a longitudinal cohort study.
items.abstract: Ethnic disparities in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) outcomes are well documented, but data on treatment response across ethnic groups remain scarce. We aimed to evaluate the effect of ethnicity on clinical outcomes following treatment escalation in a diverse UK cohort. In this longitudinal cohort study, we analysed data from the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register (BILAG-BR), including patients recruited from 64 UK secondary and tertiary rheumatology and nephrology centres. Eligible patients were aged 16 years and older, with active moderate-to-severe SLE, defined as having at least one BILAG A score, at least two BILAG B scores, or a SLEDAI-2K score of at least 6, who had initiated rituximab or belimumab within the past 12 months, or standard immunosuppressive therapy within the past 1 month. Ethnicity was categorised as White, South Asian, Black, East Asian, or mixed or other ethnicities. The primary outcome was major clinical response (MCR) at 6 months and 12 months, measured using mixed-effects logistic regression. Individuals with lived experience of SLE were involved in the study design. Between July 1, 2010, and Nov 10, 2021, 1688 patients were recruited to the BILAG-BR. Of these, 1266 were excluded because they did not meet the study eligibility criteria, and 422 patients were included in the study. 383 (91%) patients were female, 39 (9%) were male, and the median age was 40·5 years (IQR 31·3-50·8). 245 (58%) of 422 patients were White, 77 (18%) were South Asian, 70 (17%) were Black, 19 (5%) were East Asian, and 11 (3%) were of mixed or other ethnicities. At baseline, Black patients had higher baseline disease activity, greater organ damage, and more comorbidities. At 12 months, 99 (23%) of 422 patients had met MCR criteria, including eight (42%) of 19 East Asian patients, 23 (30%) of 77 South Asian patients, 60 (24%) of 245 White patients, seven (10%) of 70 Black patients, and one (9%) of 11 patients with mixed or other ethnicities. In the adjusted five-group model, patients of Black ethnicity had lower odds (OR 0·13 [95% CI 0·02-0·88]) of meeting MCR criteria compared with White patients. MCR criteria were met by fewer than a quarter of patients after treatment escalation. Patients of Black ethnicity had higher baseline disease burden and lower observed response than White patients. These results support the need for more personalised, equitable approaches to SLE management and reinforce the importance of ensuring diversity in clinical research. The British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Biologics Register who received funding support from Roche, GSK, Otsuka, and Lupus UK.

items.title: Age-stratified risk of major adverse cardiovascular events with JAK inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: A nationwide cohort study.
items.abstract: The cardiovascular safety of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) compared with biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) and conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains debated. We aimed to evaluate the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) among patients with RA initiating these therapies. We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (2010-2022). We matched adults with incident RA into JAKi, bDMARD, and csDMARD cohorts. The primary outcome was incident MACE. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs). The weighted analytic cohort included 6856 patients (814 JAKi, 1613 bDMARD, and 4429 csDMARD users). Compared with csDMARDs, overall MACE risk was lower for JAKi (aHR 0.73, 95% CI 0.54-0.99) and bDMARDs (aHR 0.60, 95% CI 0.48-0.76). While the overall MACE risk did not differ significantly between JAKi and bDMARDs (aHR 1.22, 95% CI 0.87-1.72), JAKi initiation was associated with a higher MACE risk than bDMARDs among patients with at least one cardiovascular risk factor who were aged 50 years or older (aHR 1.80, 95% CI 1.13-2.89) and 65 years or older (aHR 4.45, 95% CI 2.30-8.63). Initiating JAKi or bDMARDs lowers the overall risk of MACE compared with csDMARDs alone. However, JAKi therapy carries a significantly higher MACE risk than bDMARDs in older patients with existing cardiovascular risk factors, highlighting the need for age- and risk-stratified therapeutic selection.
